questions.label: answerable
questions.question: Why did llm implement the OpenAI Responses API as a new model class instead of modifying the existing chat completions class?
questions.reference_answer: Because the existing chat completions class had to be left untouched -- other plugins import it -- so a separate Responses model class was added, with a chat_completions boolean that dispatches back to the old implementation.

gold_citations.why: The existing chat completion class had to be left alone because other plugins import it; so a new Responses class was added, with a chat_completions boolean option to dispatch back to the old implementation.

questions.notes: Strong PR-only design rationale — docs/changelog do not explain the 'other plugins import it' reason.

questions.label: answerable
questions.question: Why does .prompt() accept an options= dict when **kwargs already worked, and why is the **kwargs form no longer documented?
questions.reference_answer: Because the maintainer intends to eventually migrate options to an options={...} form, so options= was introduced now as the documented alternative; the older **kwargs form still works for backwards-compatibility but was deliberately left undocumented to steer users toward the new form.

gold_citations.why: The maintainer wants to eventually migrate options to an options={...} form; options= was added now as a documented alternative, while the older **kwargs form is kept for backwards-compatibility but deliberately left undocumented to steer migration.

questions.notes: The 'undocument kwargs to steer migration' intent is PR-only.

questions.label: answerable
questions.question: What concrete use case drove the PauseChain primitive in llm?
questions.reference_answer: The Datasette Agent: it needed to pause a tool call mid-chain to ask for human confirmation, in a way that survives a server restart.

gold_citations.why: Needed for Datasette Agent: to pause a tool call mid-chain in order to ask for human confirmation, in a way that survives a server restart.

questions.label: answerable
questions.question: Why were async tool calls to missing/unregistered tools changed to produce error results instead of being silently dropped?
questions.reference_answer: Because a silently-dropped call left an assistant tool_call with no matching result, which OpenAI and Anthropic reject; and since chain resume landed it matters more, as a pending call whose tool is no longer registered would otherwise never resolve.

gold_citations.why: A silently-dropped call left an assistant tool_call with no matching result, which OpenAI and Anthropic reject. It matters more since chain resume landed: a pending call whose tool is no longer registered would otherwise never resolve.

questions.label: answerable
questions.question: Why does llm synthesize its own tool_call_id for providers that don't supply one, rather than leaving it empty?
questions.reference_answer: So consumers correlating tool calls with results (or keying external state on a specific invocation) don't have to invent fallback matching schemes for id-less providers, and so test models like llm-echo exercise the same code paths as production providers instead of diverging.

gold_citations.why: Consumers correlating tool calls with results (or keying external state on a specific invocation) had to invent fallback matching schemes for id-less providers, and test models like llm-echo exercised different code paths than production providers.

questions.notes: REDUNDANCY FLAG: docs/python-api.md:119 gives the correlation reason. The PR-only part is the 'llm-echo test path divergence' reason. Good case for testing PR-beats-docs retrieval; grader should require the PR citation, not accept a docs-only answer.

questions.label: answerable
questions.question: Why was a new hide_reasoning parameter added when there was already a -R/--no-reasoning option?
questions.reference_answer: Because -R/--no-reasoning was misleadingly named: it only suppressed display of reasoning text, did not actually turn reasoning off, and was not passed through to models. Since #1435 the default OpenAI plugin requests reasoning summaries, so hide_reasoning is passed through on the Prompt to let plugins opt out of requesting visible reasoning tokens.

gold_citations.why: -R/--no-reasoning was misleadingly named: it only suppressed display of reasoning text, did not turn reasoning off, and was not passed through to models. Since #1435 the default OpenAI plugin requests reasoning summaries, so hide_reasoning is passed through on the Prompt so plugins can opt not to request visible reasoning tokens.
